blinkByScore.note: Blink rate and weight follow the score band — quick and frequent when fresh, slow and heavy when wrecked

sway.note: The pair rocks a degree or so, endlessly

breathe.note: …and swells a percent on the same loop

lookAround.note: Glances off to one side and back, as if scanning

saccade.note: A one-pixel flick. Rare. Alive rather than paused

sleepAtNight.note: Past bedtime the lids sit heavy

wakeOnScore.note: Shut, then opens to the band as the number counts up

widenOnPR.note: A beat of surprise when a logged lift beats your best

wince.note: A squint when you log an injury, or a REDUCE card lands

deloadFatigue.note: Lids get heavier as a deload week wears on

restDayFace.note: Z’s float up from the mark on a rest day

markForms.note: The mark builds itself on the first load — the light comes up on the body, then the eye opens

blinkOnTap.note: Tap the mark and it blinks back

glanceAtTab.note: Looks toward the tab you just tapped — at once, or once the mark has landed if it had to fly there

scrollLook.note: Looks down as you scroll down, up as you scroll up

rollWithScore.note: The mark runs through every face and lands on the day’s as the score counts up

glanceAtNumber.note: One look down at the score after landing, then back up

nodOnSave.note: Nods when something saves; shakes when it fails

lookAtCard.note: Looks at the recommendation card you accept or dismiss

collapseSquash.note: Squashes rather than scaling flat as the header collapses

popOnArrival.note: A pop as the plate closes around it up top

busyOnGenerate.note: Scans side to side while the week is being built

firstOpenOfDay.note: Opens from shut, once, the first time you look each day

dizzySpin.note: Spins if you hammer the tabs

idleSleep.note: Nods off if you leave the app open and untouched, and wakes on your next touch

plateIsHome.note: Off Today, tapping the plate takes you back to it

busyEverywhere.note: The scan shows for anything slow, not just Generate

toastEyes.note: The toast leads with the pair, nodding or shaking, instead of a tick or a cross

glanceAtDay.note: Looks at each day as a generated week lands on the board

attentionOnCard.note: A brief look straight at you when a recommendation lands

doubleTake.note: A double blink when today jumps a long way from the last score it saw

streakPerk.note: Blinks livelier once you have a run of logged days going

blearyReturn.note: A slower, heavier open if it has been a while since you looked

timeOfDayGaze.note: Rides fractionally high in the morning, low at night

sideEye.note: A look, after three dismissals in a row

rareBeat.note: One open in a few hundred it does something you have not seen

flightTrail.note: The eyes lag the plate through the flight and catch up on landing

jelly.note: Every arrival wobbles like jelly instead of a single bounce

peek.note: Now and then it ducks below the edge and peeks back up

perEyeLag.note: The two lids move a hair apart, and not always the same one first

lidVolume.note: The eye bulges a little as it squeezes shut, like something with substance in it

lookBeforeLeaving.note: Glances where it is about to go before the flight starts

emptyStateEyes.note: Empty blocks get the pair, looking at whatever fills them

sectionBusy.note: A pair scans where a section is about to fill in, so you can see which part is thinking

gestureSmear.note: The quick gestures stretch along the way they are moving, like the flight already does

focusGaze.note: Looks at the field you are typing in

converge.note: RETIRED — the mark is one aperture in a solid, and this needs two eyes
converge.was: The two eyes turn very slightly toward each other for something close

plateSag.note: RETIRED — the plate only exists mid-flight now, so there is nothing to sag
plateSag.was: The whole plate sits lower on a bad score, not just the lids

blinkOnReturn.note: A blink when you come back to the app after a look away

impatience.note: The scan tightens when something runs longer than it should

anticipate.note: Learns which tab usually follows which, and looks at the next one

chevronEyes.note: The collapse chevrons are the mark, shut when the section is

restingPulse.note: The idle blink keeps time with your logged resting heart rate

uncertainGaze.note: Unsteady while the score is unsure, settling as the baseline matures

refusesHeld.note: Starts the glance down at a held score, then turns away instead

weekArc.note: Fresher at the start of a training week, worn by the end of it

dilate.note: The eye opens up a little in the dark

wink.note: RETIRED — the mark is one aperture in a solid, and this needs two eyes; a full close is now just a blink
wink.was: One eye, rarely, when a logged lift beats your best

sleepDebtFresh.note: RETIRED — the solid has no whites to dull; the bias carries tiredness instead
sleepDebtFresh.was: The white of the eyes dulls with your sleep debt, on Today only

looksAway.note: Closes while you are choosing your morning face, so it is not watching you answer

readsWithYou.note: Now and then, reads along a line of a long explanation you have just opened

sessionHeaviness.note: Heavier lids for the rest of the day once you have logged a real session

sittingSettles.note: The longer you are in the app in one visit, the slower the idle gets

holdGaze.note: Press and hold the mark and it looks straight at you until you let go

stayVisible.note: Perches back up in the wordmark when the score scrolls away, and drops again when it returns

colophonEyes.note: A pair on the definition at the foot of every page

tabGaze.note: Each tab sets the eyes a hair differently

lookAtToast.note: Looks at a toast when one lands

startleOnError.note: A jump, not a polite shake, when something fails

lookAtSave.note: Looks at the button you are heading for the moment a form goes dirty

thinkBeforeCard.note: A beat of looking away before a recommendation lands

lookAtPanel.note: Looks at a panel that opens over the page

tabWander.note: Glances at the tab bar if you sit on one tab a long time

glitch.note: Now and then the pair tears for a moment, the way it blinks

chipBlinks.note: The docked face blinks on its own clock — set by what you told it, not by what the score says

chipAndMark.note: The pair and the docked face notice each other now and then, and what passes between them depends on whether they agree

tearOnFlight.note: The mark tears as it lands — flying between the wordmark and the score, and perching as you scroll past it

EYE_NO_PREVIEW.rareBeat: One open in a few hundred
EYE_NO_PREVIEW.jelly: Any time the mark pops in
EYE_NO_PREVIEW.peek: Now and then, on its own

traceDraw.note: The trend chart draws its line, and the band fills in behind it

loadTilt.note: A week that beat its plan pushes past the tick and rocks back

gapDots.note: The trend line goes dotted across a gap where you logged nothing

dayHandoff.note: Midnight passing with the app open turns the date over

firstLight.note: Your first generated week arrives a day at a time

strikeThrough.note: A drill you tick is struck through rather than switching to done

sessionProgress.note: The drill count carries a bar that fills as you cross them off

staleBreath.note: A section that has gone stale exhales once when you land on it

overscroll.note: The page stretches at the top and springs back

flipReorder.note: Reordered goals slide past each other instead of teleporting

chipActsOut.note: A card’s chip acts out its own symbol as the card lands

rankFlip.note: A goal’s rank turns over when its place changes

cardExit.note: Accepted cards settle in, dismissed ones flick away

collapseMotion.note: Sections open and close instead of blinking in and out

growBars.note: Bars grow from nothing, one after another

digitRoll.note: The score rolls its digits like a counter

digitStep.note: …and the counter ticks between digits rather than sliding through them

scoreGlitch.note: A day you swipe to tears itself in rather than simply appearing

markGlitch.note: How long the mark's own tear lasts — whether it happens at all is the eyes' own row

tickLevel.note: Ticking a level in a picker lands with a beat

rungFill.note: Ticking a rung fills the ones under it in order rather than all at once

landsWhereSent.note: A section a card sent you to draws its own rule down as you arrive

budgetBar.note: Today’s session carries a bar showing its length against your setting

weightsDrift.note: Each channel’s bar travels from its starting weight to the one your data learned

streakBurst.note: The mark throws confetti the first time you log on a new day

staggerIn.note: List entries arrive one after another rather than all at once

toastFrom.note: The toast comes from wherever you just tapped

panelDirection.note: A panel arrives from the side its tab sits on — what runs when the deal is off, since both write the same transform

tabIndicator.note: The light runs along the tab bar to where you tapped, rather than jumping there

rowRemove.note: A removed row closes up instead of vanishing

crossFade.note: A redrawn detail fades rather than hard-swaps

fieldUnderline.note: A focused field draws its underline in from the left

buttonPress.note: Buttons press down under the finger

headerHairline.note: A hairline appears under the header once the page has scrolled

bannerSlide.note: The update banner slides down rather than appearing

skeleton.note: Waiting shows the shape of what is coming, pulsing

stickyHeads.note: A section’s heading sticks to the top while you read it

tabLift.note: A new page is dealt in from the side you swiped, over the app’s own black

planDeal.note: A generated week is dealt out day by day rather than appearing whole

pillExtend.note: A section’s title pill extends out as the page lands, rather than arriving whole

facesRollIn.note: The five faces roll in as balls when the question is put to you

firstRunThread.note: The setup questions arrive one at a time, each as the last is answered

fieldDrift.note: A dot field ripples half a wave through, in the direction you swiped, once its page has landed

APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.460: A skill opens on its whole ladder, not two rungs and a “show all”.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.461: Injuries is a heading and a button until something hurts.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.462: Logging an injury asks all six things the same way instead of three and a form.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.463: Every field in the app is outlined instead of a white box.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.464: An answer you type is set like an answer you pick.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.465: You can log an injury from Today, where you are when something twinges.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.466: The Log an injury button on Today is a real button, and it actually opens the sheet.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.467: Log an injury wears the app’s injury red on Today.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.468: A session can no longer give you the same lift twice under two names.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.469: The exercise list holds one entry per exercise — six lifts that had been entered twice are one entry each now.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.470: A Log button in the masthead, on every tab — and it can start a workout that was never planned.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.471: Logging is a popup now, the same shape as everything else in the app, and it opens from anywhere.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.472: The masthead button is a plus.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.473: You can log a workout you did days ago — the popup steps back a day at a time.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.474: A workout you have logged counts as being set up — Today stops asking you to build a week.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.475: Start typing a lift and it offers the ones you already do, then the rest of the library.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.476: A lift you entered yourself keeps the sets and reps you gave it instead of being re-prescribed.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.477: The weight box takes a set at a time — 60,80,100 for a ramp, or a drop set, or a back-off.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.478: The plus sits in the middle of the masthead beside the mark, and tucks into the corner as you scroll.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.479: Type different reps and weights per set and the row says back what it read, set by set.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.480: Different reps and weights per set: the row says back what it read, set by set.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.481: The log button is a disc at the bottom of Today, where your thumb already is.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.482: The log button is the size of the mark, and sits on the page without a ring around it.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.483: On Today the mark no longer hides in the masthead — it falls to the bottom of the page and opens as the log button.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.484: The mark flies to the mark, one at a time — the drop lands where it should now.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.485: The black mark stays out of the masthead on Today, however you got there.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.486: The log button is a proper size — and the mark stays mark-sized on the way down to it.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.487: The mark flies on nothing again — the cream plate behind it is gone.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.10.488: The mark carries a hairline, everywhere it is drawn.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.11.489: The mark’s edge has weight, and sits off register against wherever it is looking.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.11.490: Coming back to Today no longer flashes the black mark in the masthead before the coloured one returns.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.11.491: The five faces you rate the day with are big enough to hit — and big enough to tell apart.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.492: Logging a session asks you what you did, in the voice the rest of the app asks things in — and the whole session fits on one screen.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.493: Which half of the day you are logging reads at a glance.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.494: The log sheet is set in four sizes and two faces, and each face means something.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.495: The mark keeps your colour the whole way up from the log button.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.496: The log sheet names each session instead of calling them AM and PM.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.497: On Data, the six things to chart and the three ways to draw them stop looking like one keypad of nine.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.498: The dot field is thinner — wider rows, more space along each one, a lighter ink.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.500: Section headers go back to the band and box they had before.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.501: The five faces take their colours from the new palette, and get their light-to-dark order back.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.502: The masthead carries a tint of the tab you are on.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.503: The five faces you pick from are five expressions, not five heights of the same one.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.504: The mark wears the face you picked, not just its colour.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.12.505: Today drops its Log this workout button — the disc at the bottom already does it.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.13.506: The tab’s tint is the masthead’s alone — the warm-up and cool-down keep their rule and give up their fill.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.13.507: Every section sits on the ground now, on every tab — the tint is the masthead’s and nothing else’s.

meta_analysis.label: META-ANALYSIS
meta_analysis.note: Backed by a pooled analysis of many studies — the strongest evidence here.

systematic_review.label: REVIEW
systematic_review.note: Backed by a formal review of the published research.

rct.label: RCT
rct.note: Backed by a randomised controlled trial — one good study rather than many.

coaching_consensus.label: CONSENSUS
coaching_consensus.note: What coaches broadly agree on, rather than a lab finding. Useful, just a different kind of evidence.

strength.label: Strength — work toward a top set of ~5, or 5×5/3×5. Bigger jumps, lower reps.

hypertrophy.label: Hypertrophy — 3×8-12 or 4×8-10. Progress reps within range before adding weight.

power.label: Power — low reps, high intent, full rest between sets. Weight increases are small and infrequent — technical quality matters more than the number.

SKILL_TO_INTEGRATE.pike: Bear crawl to downward dog flow

RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.easy: Walk, then run the first kilometre slower than target pace — that is the warm-up
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.recovery: Walk, then run the first kilometre slower than target pace — that is the warm-up
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.long: Easy jog to open up, starting slower than feels necessary — 5-10 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.tempo: Easy jog, last 2 minutes lifting toward steady — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.hills: Easy jog to the hill, then one relaxed uphill at half effort — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.sprint: Easy jog. Never sprint cold — 15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.race: Easy jog, finishing 25-30 min before the start — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.race_long: Easy jog to loosen off, finishing 15-20 min before the start — 5-10 min. The opening kilometres are the rest of the warm-up

RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.easy: Walk, then ease into the first kilometre slower than target pace. The run is the warm-up.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.long: 5-10 min easy jog to open up, then settle. Start slower than feels necessary.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.tempo: 10-15 min easy jog, last 2 min lifting toward steady · 4-6 × 80-100m strides · first rep within 2 min.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.interval: 10-15 min easy jog · 4-6 × 80-100m strides at target pace · rep one within 2 min.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.fartlek: 10 min easy jog · 3 × 20s strides. The first surge is the warm-up for the rest.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.hills: 10-15 min easy jog to the hill · one relaxed uphill at half effort before the working reps.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.sprint: 15 min easy jog · 4-6 progressive strides. Never sprint cold.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.race: 10-15 min easy jog finishing 25-30 min out · 4-6 strides · keep moving with layers on, gap to the gun under 5 min. At half or full marathon distance cut the jog to 5-10 min and treat the first kilometres as the rest of it.
